body:
**Michael Bayer ([@zzzeek](https://github.com/zzzeek)) wrote:**

compare() is not implemented for many items:


```
C = Cartoon.age.label("X")
D = Cartoon.age.label("X")

assert C.compare(D)
```

the test suite itself does not rely upon this method.  Stick to the str() approach which is what the test suite does right now also.

**Changes by Michael Bayer ([@zzzeek](https://github.com/zzzeek)):**

* changed **title** from "BooleanClauseList.compare fails when an expression" to "clauseelement.compare() is not implemented for cas"

**miso ([@mbarakaja](https://github.com/mbarakaja)) wrote:**

Thanks for the quick response.

rename.from: clauseelement.compare() is not implemented for cast(), label(), many others
rename.to: clauseelement.compare() is not implemented for cast(), label(), many others, consider deprecation

body:
the compare() methods aren't used anywhere except as assertion points in test/sql/test_operators.py.   they are also used in some brief spots inside of orm/relationships.py and orm/strategies.py.

we don't have the resources to support having these methods being fully public and working in every case, so maybe should be deprecated in 1.4?  however the ORM case makes this more complicated.   At the very least we need to define as far as the ORM what the scope of these .compare() methods is meant to be, since we know for example they dont cover FROM clauses, they cover ColumnElement but not things like cast(), is that actually a bug above re: the way the ORM uses compare()?    what if there is a binary condition like "cast(A) == cast(A)" ?   on this issue we need to at least figure out if the incompleteness in compare() can actually affect the ORM, and if not, why not, can that help us with compare().

I tried doing this:

```diff
diff --git a/test/orm/test_relationships.py b/test/orm/test_relationships.py
index 652b8bacd6..1ee1998c47 100644
--- a/test/orm/test_relationships.py
+++ b/test/orm/test_relationships.py
@@ -886,20 +886,21 @@ class CompositeSelfRefFKTest(fixtures.MappedTest, AssertsCompiledSQL):
                 "reports_to": relationship(
                     Employee,
                     primaryjoin=sa.and_(
-                        employee_t.c.emp_id == employee_t.c.reports_to_id,
-                        employee_t.c.company_id == employee_t.c.company_id,
+                        remote(employee_t.c.emp_id) == foreign(employee_t.c.reports_to_id),
+                        func.cast(employee_t.c.company_id, Integer) == remote(foreign(func.cast(employee_t.c.company_id, Integer))),
+                        #employee_t.c.company_id == employee_t.c.company_id,
                     ),
-                    remote_side=[employee_t.c.emp_id, employee_t.c.company_id],
-                    foreign_keys=[
-                        employee_t.c.reports_to_id,
-                        employee_t.c.company_id,
-                    ],
+#                    remote_side=[employee_t.c.emp_id, employee_t.c.company_id],
+                    #foreign_keys=[
+                    #    employee_t.c.reports_to_id,
+                    #    employee_t.c.company_id,
+                    #],
                     backref=backref(
                         "employees",
-                        foreign_keys=[
-                            employee_t.c.reports_to_id,
-                            employee_t.c.company_id,
-                        ],
+                     #   foreign_keys=[
+                     #       employee_t.c.reports_to_id,
+                     #       employee_t.c.company_id,
+                     #   ],
                     ),
                 ),
             },

```

but once you have the annotations, which are needed in any case for the functional ON clause, it no longer needs compare().  the compare() is also used when it figures out the "get clause" thing and maybe I can find a way for the lack of .compare() to trigger that.

however, it's clear the ORM needs .compare() in a few cases and it's not sufficient that a new ColumnElement can be added that has a non-working compare() on it.    

I would like to have .compare() be local to ColumnElement.  However at the moment, ClauseList is not a ColumnElement.   Maybe it shoudl be.

So I think the steps should be:

1. consider that compare() becomes local to ColumnElement.  deprecate it on base ClauseElement, but only if we can turn ClauseList into ColumnElement which might be a way bigger deal. 

1a.  alternatively, have the base compare() raise NotImplementedError().

2. new test suite, walks the entire subclass hierarchy of ColumnElement and ensures a test fixture exists which generates two different samples of that object.    The samples will then be used in a compare() test (both equals and not equals).  While we're at it, we can write tests for copy_internals() also.    "test_column_element.py".  this way when new ColumnElement objects are added, the test suite will fail until the required tests are added.

3. fix the comparisons here which in this case conform to Cast, but they also dont work for other Function / FunctionElement, etc.

**Mike Bayer** has proposed a fix for this issue in the **master** branch:

**Implement .compare() for all ColumnElements** https://gerrit.sqlalchemy.org/1195

so I've gone through this huge exercise in the gerrit above to make a comprehensive "compare()" that works everywhere, ran the tests and ran straight into a huge wall that the ORM is using a very specialized set of rules in ColumnElement.compare() that make it behave in entirely not how a normal "compare()" would work.

so again, we are faced with the ORM having a very specific, non-generic, limited form of compare() that's basically used in two little places with column-only expressions of very limited scope.

the problem with compare is that it is not clear how many elements should be compared.  If I have bindparam(None, 'x') and bindparam(None, 'x'), should they compare as True or False?  If I have two Table objects, everything is the same except one is a copy of the other, do they compare as True or False?    we need to compare tables because: we need to compare columns, which means we need to compare ScalarSelects, which means we need to compare selects(), which means tables.     The above gerrit ended up being very complicated.   Then when we figure there should be flags for all kinds of options, like compare tables and columns on identitty or their contents?  compare anonymous labels and bind parameters on identity or not? it becomes an enormously complex feature for which *there is no official use case* we are trying to suit.

so after spending hours today above I am again leaning towards "deprecate"; the ORM's use of compare() should be moved to an ORM-only function that runs a visitors.traverse() on both elements, and then runs it's very particular kinds of rules when it encounters ColumnElement or BinaryExpression, which is pretty much all it cares about, and then it's done.

**Mike Bayer** has proposed a fix for this issue in the **rel_2_0** branch:

**Reimplement .compare() in terms of a visitor** https://gerrit.sqlalchemy.org/1198

issue.title: create new baked select (generic caching for all Core / ORM executable constructs)

labels.name: alchemy 2
labels.description: goes along with the 2.0 milestone to aid in searching

issue.body:
see the proof of concept in https://gist.github.com/zzzeek/1f7bd3cc19e7ebea8f364e5b40577067

however this also needs to integrate with the "selector select" #4636 , which may or may not be a transparent process (e.g. run the lambdas, build the select, etc.)

It also might be useful that the new baked select can do the "selector" process just like the "selector select" does, since we are already looking at lambdas.   Lets have the initial lambda hook scan the objects being called upon, and then do the Core/ORM switch based on those objects we see.   Then there can be an ORM baked select and a Core baked select.
